hook: Tonight you can study for a test or work a shift that pays \$80. Choose the test, and the cost is not zero: it is the \$80 you did not earn. Countries face the same kind of choice, only bigger: more tractors means less wheat. The production possibilities curve puts that choice on a graph.

options: Wants are greater than the resources to meet them
A store has run out of a product
prereq.why: Scarcity is the gap between unlimited wants and limited resources.

prereq.q: A curve that bows outward from the origin has a slope that
options: gets steeper as it falls toward the horizontal axis
prereq.why: A bowed-out curve starts flat and gets steeper as it falls.

prereq.why: Capital is made goods used in production.

figure.caption: Points on the PPC are efficient, U inside shows idle resources, Z outside is out of reach now, and PPC2 shows growth from more resources or better technology.

chain.cause: An economy uses all its resources efficiently
chain.effect: it produces at a point on its PPC

chain.cause: It moves along the PPC to make more of one good
chain.effect: it gives up some of the other good: the opportunity cost

chain.cause: Resources are not equally suited to both goods
chain.effect: each extra unit costs more of the other good, so the PPC bows outward
the whole PPC shifts outward, and points once out of reach become possible

ideas: Opportunity cost: the value of the next-best alternative given up. Per unit, it is what you give up divided by what you gain.
On the PPC: efficient. Inside: idle or misused resources (a recession). Outside: unattainable with today's resources and technology.
Bowed out means increasing opportunity cost (specialized resources); a straight line means constant opportunity cost.
More resources or better technology shift the PPC outward; a disaster shifts it inward. Moving resources between the two goods is a movement along it.

misconception.wrong: Putting idle factories back to work shifts the PPC outward.
misconception.right: Idle resources put the economy inside its PPC; using them moves the economy toward the curve. Only more resources or better technology shift the curve itself outward.

summary: Opportunity cost is the next-best alternative you give up, and the production possibilities curve shows it for a whole economy: every point on the curve is efficient, points inside mean idle resources, and points outside are out of reach for now. A bowed-out PPC means increasing opportunity cost, a straight one constant cost. More resources or better technology shift the curve outward; moving resources from one good to the other is a movement along it.
